commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 generalize (PR #1300): decouples component gates from exemplar flags; PR body says the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — logic/scope correction to 100 merged generated modules.
description: never again zeroed by China-list or aluminum membership (the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins)

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The §122 temporary-import-surcharge exemption branch fired on the witness's exemplar line flags (`if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0`), so it zeroed the 10% surcharge for every China-301-listed line regardless of origin and tied the genuine §232 carve-out to one aluminum exemplar row, whereas the cited proclamation excludes only the Annex I/II product categories and articles subject to §232 restrictions.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 12; verified line-by-line that every added/removed formula line is identical to ch13 after normalizing the chapter prefix and the generator's redundant-parenthesis count. Only serialization style differs: this chapter uses `effective_from:` where ch13 uses `from:` (a placement-gate distinctness device, no meaning change). Same caveats as index 12: partial decoupling (entry_is_line_d and the IEEPA `not entry_is_line_b` survive), new steel component added rather than a corrected value, and the steel rule's double-nested metadata.proof.proof.atoms is repaired later in a14f43975.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a caller-interface rename or as new pilot coverage, and it does not hold: the §122 zero branch's own proof atoms (byte-identical pre and post) ground it only on "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and on "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04" — nothing in the cited §122 sources conditions the exemption on China-301 list membership. Pre-fix the branch fired on `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b`, and the very same module used those two booleans as the China-301 list-1 and 2024-action gates (`if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate`), so on a chapter-wide surface one boolean cannot simultaneously mean "on the §122 exclusion list" and "on China 301 list 1" — at least one branch necessarily disagrees with its cited source for every non-exemplar line, which is exactly the harm the PR records ("unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins") and books as a deliberate value-changing exception class in the witness-equivalence gate. The fix re-grounds the predicate on `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered` and applies the same re-grounding to the §232-aluminum, §201, Brazil-301 and forced-labor-301 gates, so encoded meaning changed and untraceable_branch ("a condition with no basis in the cited source... the fix re-grounds it") is the right kind.

triage.verifier_notes: Kept the first reader's kind, but their stated reading is slightly off on one detail: `entry_is_line_a` is the reciprocal-annex-excluded exemplar (module derives `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a`, HTS 7202.11.10 ferroalloy) and `entry_is_line_b` the aluminum exemplar (`entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded`). The defect is the conflation, not a literally China-keyed predicate: the same two flags doubled as the China-301 list-1 and 2024-action gates, so whichever membership entry preparation supplied, one branch was ungrounded. A reviewer could reasonably prefer wrong_entity_or_scope (exemption applied to the wrong article population); I judged untraceable_branch better because the branch condition itself, not the entity/period, lacked source basis and the fix re-grounds rather than re-scopes it. Two caveats for pruning: (1) this commit mixes in genuine non-defect work — the new `ch14_s232_steel_heading_rate` / `section_232_steel_component_rate` and the extra `+ section_232_steel_component_rate` stack term are new coverage the module never claimed (PR: the witness's ferroalloy sits outside note 16(c)), so do not count the steel addition as the defect; the Brazil/forced-labor edits add a missing `entry_is_*_listed` membership condition and would read as unrepresented_clause if scored separately. (2) The new steel rule in this commit's bytes has malformed doubly-nested `metadata: proof: proof: atoms:`, repaired later per the PR issue comment ("steel atoms unwrapped to canonical `metadata.proof.atoms`") — cosmetic to this classification. Provenance note: the §122 exception atom cites `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221` for "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03", but that page in the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS 2026 Rev 3) contains 9903.01.77 notes (x)-(z), not subdivision (aa); the §122 exclusion list text was not resolvable in the pinned release, so the source check rests on the surcharge proclamation atom (FR 2026-03824, "on articles imported into the United States") plus the unchanged §232-metals exception atom. Those atoms also still cite the exemplar line "7202.11.10" after the formula was generalized.
